title: Stalk of the compactly supported direct image
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $\pi:E\to B$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(E,\Lambda)$, and let
$\bar b\to B$ be a geometric
point with the fiber $E_{\bar b}$. The canonical comparison

$$
(R\pi_!K)_{\bar b}\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;R\Gamma_c(E_{\bar b},K|_{E_{\bar b}})
$$

is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Use the literal pullback X_s = X times_Y Spec Omega and the base-changed compactification c.baseChange s. The unchanged definitions compactFiberProperSquare and compactFiberOpenSquare supply the proper and open Cartesian squares. The unchanged four Lean statements already express the stalk/fibre formula as invertibility of their specified exchange arrows on Spec Omega, so no further stalk or endpoint comparison is needed in these proofs.

At finite coefficients, extract bounds a and b from intrinsic bounded constructibility. Cohomology vanishes outside [min(a,b),b]. Apply lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin to obtain a bounded constructible etale complex L and its intrinsic-realization isomorphism to K. Undo intrinsic realization with the unit of sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence and the canonical derived-composition isomorphism. The lower bound of L supplies its D-plus membership. Apply the published ProEtale.isIso_rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationBaseChangeMap_app to this bounded-below etale-origin witness and the literal pullback square. Its arrow is definitionally compactFiberFiniteMap. This is the finite-level compact-support base-change route, with proper and open factors packaged by that published theorem.

At integral coefficients, finite type over the fixed field gives Noetherianness and finite Krull dimension of X. The coefficient prime is a unit in each stalk by the purity setting, and hence a unit in global sections. Apply integralStratifiedPerfectDetailed, the detailed-category clause of lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization, to K. This gives bounded constructible complete membership of its unchanged integralDetailedTransport image, including compatible etale-origin reductions. For every requested generating tuple, the general auxiliary theorem wfConstructible_complete of def-wf-tensor-product gives cbcCompleteProperty: WfIsComplete and cbcCompleteProperty use exactly the same intrinsic unit and canonical representative. Apply completeCompactSupportProetale_isIso to this object and its compatible origins. Project its first conclusion to obtain invertibility of the exact completedCompactSupportExchange displayed in compactFiber_integral. No new coefficient object or map is chosen.

A raw rational object has its original integral constructible object K.obj. Repeat Step 3 for that object; no finite-Tor input is needed by the completed exchange theorem. Localize the resulting invertible completedCompactSupportExchange by the actual ScalarLocalization.localization functor in the unchanged statement. Functors preserve isomorphisms, giving compactFiber_rational. This uses the integral representative directly and does not require a separate rational-transport theorem.

For Qbar, finite type gives Noetherianness of X, Y and the geometric fibre, and finite dimension of X, Y, Spec Omega and the geometric fibre. Base change supplies finite type of the fibre projection; the purity setting gives invertibility of the coefficient prime on all four schemes. Specialize qbarCompactSupportBaseChange to c, c.baseChange s and the literal proper/open squares. Its first conclusion supplies Nonempty of the normalized exchange model, without choosing a model as data. For every model D and object K, project its descended-component IsIso conclusion. These are exactly the two conclusions of CompactFiberQbarFormula. All four proofs retain the given canonical maps and therefore apply to zero inputs, empty fibres and identity squares without exceptional choices.

split_report.summary: Expanded the imported compactification argument into five steps. Step 1 fixes the base-changed compactification and identifies the stalk as the geometric-point inverse-image fibre. Step 2 applies finite-level pro-etale compact-support base change to an etale-origin witness and identifies the proper fibre term with the geometric-fibre formula. Steps 3 and 4 spell out the integral, rational, and common-stage coefficient transports using the completed tower realization, finite-extension base change, and Qbar descent. Step 5 records canonicality, naturality, and edge cases. No new nodes were needed; every cited statement was checked against its recorded hypotheses. Maintainer review (2026-10-18): Steps 1, 3 and 4 were repaired. Step 1 now defines the fibre square, $R\Gamma_c$ and the stalk reading. Step 3 now cites the identification of the integral categories, the completeness of $j_!$, the extension-by-zero limit presentation and the direct-image limit comparison that match the completed exchange with the tower definition of $R\pi_!$. Step 4 now cites the identification of the purity rational and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ categories with the proper-base-change ones before applying thm-cbc-finite-extension and thm-cbc-qbar.

lean.note: The four coefficient clauses are compactFiber_finite, _integral, _rational and _qbar. Each states invertibility of the specified compactification exchange over the geometric point, the stalk/fibre reading fixed by Step 1 of this node. Integral input is the original detailed finite-Tor object transported by integralDetailedTransport. Rational input is the original raw sfRationalConstructibleCategory, and its map is actual localization of the completed arrow. The Qbar clause uses the published unit/scalar-normalized common-stage model and asserts its existence; no model is an extra hypothesis. Helpers construct only the literal proper/open fibre squares and specialize existing canonical maps. All chapter hypotheses are retained explicitly by include; no new coefficient category, arbitrary comparison or proof is introduced.
